finding.claim: Helpers.sanitize intends to remove <form> elements, but its XPath './form' only matches direct children of the fragment root. Nested forms survive with their action attribute and input fields, which enables credential-phishing form injection.
finding.source:
Attacker-controlled HTML input to Loofah::Helpers.sanitize, e.g.
.
finding.sink: Protected operation: the sanitizer's form-removal guarantee (output must contain no form elements). The surviving form is rendered in the victim's page and submits to the attacker's origin.

trace.note: scrub!(:strip): form is in ACCEPTABLE_ELEMENTS (safelist.rb:89), so Strip keeps it and the nested form survives strip
allowed_element?: form is allowed, so attributes are scrubbed rather than the element removed
action is in ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES (safelist.rb:237) and in ATTR_VAL_IS_URI (safelist.rb:583); https://evil.example passes allowed_uri? (scrub.rb:170-186) and is kept
xpath('./form') matches only direct children of the fragment, so the nested <form> inside <div> is not removed
to_s emits the nested form, input and button

finding.guards_checked: (1) Strip scrubber: keeps form (form, input and button are on the safelist). (2) attribute scrubbing: action is allowed and https:// is a permitted protocol. (3) The explicit form-removal step at line 24 is the only control, and it is scoped too narrowly. Severity depends on whether form removal is an intended guarantee of Helpers.sanitize; the code clearly attempts it, so I treat it as in-scope.
